newsitem.title: USA: U.S. anti-drug chief to visit Colombian police.
newsitem.headline: U.S. anti-drug chief to visit Colombian police.

text.p: U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration chief Thomas Constantine will visit Colombia next Tuesday to check out the lastest trends in cocaine trafficking, a DEA spokesman said.
On his first visit to Colombia, Constantine will meet with General Rosso Jose Serrano, chief of the National Police, which heads the counter-narcotics war, and his top advisers.
Constantine will present a plaque honouring Colombian officers who have died fighting the illegal drug trade.
"He is going there to discuss current trends and what they see as the changing dynamic of the trafficking situation in Colombia," the spokesman said.

The DEA chief will discuss what the Colombian cartels are up to and the impact of the death of Mexico's top trafficker, Amado Carillo Fuentes, head of the Juarez cartel and a major transporter of Colombian cocaine, the spokesman said.
Carrillo Fuentes died mysteriously on July 4 after undergoing liposuction in a plastic surgery operation.
Constantine's one day visit will take place as Colombia's Congress reopens debate on a bill to lift a 6-year-old ban on extraditing Colombian citizens to stand trial abroad.
"He will probably also be discussing certification," the DEA spokesman added.
In March, the U.S. government blacklisted or "decertified" Colombia for a second consecutive year for failing to crack down hard enough on drug trafficking.
U.S. anti-drug officials consider Colombian President Ernesto Samper to be corrupt for allegedly using drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.
The DEA estimates Colombia still provides about 80 percent of the world's cocaine supply and has become the main supplier of high-grade heroin to the United States.
